entries.reason: ADAPTED in the launch and in nothing else. The source is `monkeypatch.setattr(hook_module, "read_fence", boom)` followed by an in-process `main([...])`. The port's equivalent of the monkeypatch is a replacement of `hookSeams.readFence` (D-0014), and that is what happens -- but `main()` reads stdin synchronously to EOF before it reaches the fence, exactly as `sys.stdin.read()` does, so calling it inside the runner would block on the runner's own stdin whenever that is a terminal. So the seam is replaced and `main()` is called inside a child Node process whose stdin is closed. The source's assertion is kept in full (`main` RETURNED `EXIT_DENY`, read back from a file the child writes, with `EXIT_DENY` taken from the hook module rather than hard-coded), and the case is STRONGER for the adaptation: the child's own exit status is asserted too, which is the thing the case is named for and would be 1 if the error had escaped as a traceback.

entries.target_id: test/fencing/deny-hook.test.ts::the fence must belong to the role > a fence for another role is denied
entries.reason: STRENGTHENED, and only in the direction the rulebook requires. The source asserts `"curator" in decision.reason and "worker" in decision.reason`; the port asserts both names in their QUOTED form (`'curator'`, `'worker'`), which is how the hook interpolates them through the Python `repr` transcription. A bare substring test is unfalsifiable here: the same reason carries the fence PATH, and the path is built from the per-case temporary root, so a root that happened to contain the word would satisfy the source's assertion against a hook that never named a role at all. That is the D-0020 failure mode, in the one file whose refusal message is built from a path the case itself chose. The property pinned is the source's; the assertion is a superset of it.

entries.reason: The source's last class differs from the rest of its file by LAUNCH MECHANISM: every other case runs the hook as `python -m claude_org_runtime.fencing.hook`, and these run the command string the renderer emits, which invokes the file BY PATH -- the difference that once hid a real hole (relative imports failing with ImportError and exit 1). Node has no `-m`, and `hook.mjs` is only ever launched by path (D-0204), so in the port both launches collapse onto `node <hook.mjs>` and this class no longer differs by mechanism. It is kept because it still varies everything else it was written to vary -- the argv comes out of the rendered settings through `shlex.split`, the child runs in a foreign working directory, and the environment is stripped -- and the source's `_clean_env` (which pops PYTHONPATH so the package is deliberately not importable from the child) becomes removal of NODE_PATH and NODE_OPTIONS, the two variables that can add a module search root or inject a loader. STRENGTHENED to re-secure what the collapse costs: the case additionally asserts the payload's `interlock.rule_id` equals the probe's rule id. Interlock's hook EXITS 1 when it cannot load itself, so the source's `returncode != 1` distinguishes "the fence denied this probe" from "the hook could not load"; continuo's hook denies with 2 in both cases, so without the rule-id assertion an unloadable hook would satisfy every other assertion in the case.

inherited_limitations.topic: `returncode != 1` no longer distinguishes a fence deny from a hook that could not load, because this hook's deny status is 2 rather than interlock's 1.
inherited_limitations.status: translation hazard, found and closed inside this file rather than left open
inherited_limitations.detail: interlock's hook exits 1 when it cannot load itself, so the source's `returncode != 1` is exactly what separates "the fence denied this probe" from "the hook broke and denied by default". continuo's hook denies with exit 2 (D-0204/D-0207), so a straight translation of `returncode != 1` plus `decision == "block"` is satisfied by a hook that never read a fence. Two cases in the rendered-command class -- "the rendered command denies a probe" and "every role rendered command runs" -- therefore carry an added assertion that the denied `rule_id` is the PROBE's rule id, which only a hook that actually read the published fence can produce. The added assertion is a strengthening in the direction the rulebook requires, not a divergence: it pins the property the source's exit-code check pinned on its own runtime. Cross-reference: this is one of three cases in this port where the suite was green while proving nothing; the three are written up together in docs/test-translation-conventions.md, section 9 ("Make it fail on purpose, and confirm it fails for the reason you expect").
